documentNotes.title: Instructions
documentNotes.statement:
1. Do not open the exam envelop yourself.
2. This part of the exam involves observation with real sky. You must complete two tasks using the equipment provided.
3. Hand the exam envelope to the proctor at the exam station.
4. You have 6 minutes to complete the first task, and 4 minutes to complete the second task.
5. Once you complete a task, call out to the proctor to have it graded.
6. Once graded, that answer is considered final and you may not return to it again.
7. Once the timer has expired any ungraded task will be graded as is. (So make sure you complete the task before the timer has elapsed)

transcription.notes: Page 1 prints the general instructions (kept in paper.documentNotes). Instruction 1 prints “envelop” where “envelope” is meant; “envelop” is an English word, so it is kept as printed. Page 6 (star-trail photograph, “Note: provided at exam station”) does not say which task it belongs to; it is attached to N2 after the page-5 sky map. The page-5 sky map is marked as not provided to the examinees. No points are printed; timeLimitMin 10 is the sum of the printed 6 minutes (first task) and 4 minutes (second task). The student-code boxes, the masthead and the logos are not figures. There is no solutions document.

problems.title: N1: Observation with Equatorial Mount Telescope
problems.statement:
**Instruction:** Use the Equatorial Mount Telescope to observe the target given in the star chart. Write down the **Name** and make sure the target is **focused**.

**Included:**

- Equatorial Mount Telescope
- Mount is already polar aligned
- Eyepiece: 25 mm
- Finder scope already aligned with the main scope
- Telescope starts already pointing at “starting star” (see map)
- Star chart with starting and target position marked.

Target name: ________________________________________

figures.caption: Note: To be provided attached to a clipboard at exam station
figures.alt: Star atlas chart number 6 covering right ascension 0h to about 2h50m and declination +8° to +45° (Andromeda, Triangulum, Pisces, Aries), with a stellar magnitude legend, double and variable star symbols, and labelled stars Almaak, Mirach, Alpheratz, Hamal, Sheratan, Mesarthim and Algenib. Mirach (β And) is circled in dark blue and labelled “Starting star”; an empty region near ν And is circled and labelled “Target” in red.

problems.title: N2: Observation with Dobsonian Telescope
problems.statement:
**Instruction:** Use the Dobsonian Telescope provided to observe **only one** of the following objects and **focus** on selected object.

|  | Name | Bayer Designation |
|---|---|---|
| ☐ | Menkar | α Cet |
| ☐ | Markab | α Peg |
| ☐ | Hamal | α Ari |
| ☐ | Fomalhaut | α PsA |
| ☐ | Alpheratz | α And |

**Included:**

- Dobsonian Telescope
- Eyepiece: 12 and 25 mm
- Finder scope is already aligned with main scope.

The status bar reads “FOV 187°   50.2 FPS   2017-11-14 21:00:00 UTC+07:00”.
